scenes.title: Companion Scan
scenes.caption: Walk the room. Keep the map.
scenes.narration: The scan leaves your phone. It lands on your own server.

scenes.caption: Two ways in. Both end in a map.
scenes.narration: Scan a room with the camera, or upload a walkthrough video you already have.

shots.alt: Start screen offering two equal paths: scan a room, or upload a video

scenes.caption: Camera sees the room. You walk it slowly.
scenes.narration: The camera sees the room, motion tracks you, and a slow sweep keeps tracking locked.

shots.alt: First onboarding step explaining that Companion Scan needs camera and motion access
shots._focusNote:
The five onboarding cards are the only shots in the film where the subject is a small object on a large empty ground. The modal measures w 0.24 x h 0.45 of the plate and sits dead centre; the rest of the 16:9 frame is unlit app shell that carries nothing. Unfocused, the body copy renders at about a 10px x-height on a 1080p frame — technically present, actually unread. The 9:16 cut has no such problem and gets NO focus: the phone frame already crops to the card.

0.64 square at (0.18, 0.18), 2.016x, honoured exactly — deliberately looser than the 0.538 the clamp would allow. At 0.538 (the tightest 16:9 permits) the window anchors and slices the card's icon off the top edge, the same guillotine described in the promise focus note on the spatial-companion film. At 0.60 the whole card fits but 'Skip tutorial' lands on the caption band. 0.64 clears both. Same rect on all five so the cards read as one carousel being paged through rather than five unrelated pushes.

shots.alt: Second onboarding step, Sweep the Room Slowly, explaining that moving too fast degrades SLAM tracking and that the live point cloud shows what has been covered

scenes.caption: Thin at first. Full as you walk.
scenes.narration: Walk the room and the map fills in, with coverage scored live as you go.

shots.alt: The scanning HUD a few seconds into the walk, with a thin point count, a low coverage bar and the live quality recommendation the app raises for a sparse map
The same scanning HUD later in the walk, with the point count in the thousands and the coverage bar reading Good

scenes.caption: Every object named, placed and yours.
scenes.narration: Objects come back named and placed, identified on hardware you own.

shots.alt: The Latest scan readout over the camera feed, listing objects this capture found with a label, a confidence figure and a 3D position each
The object manifest at the top of the side panel, counting the objects found and listing each one with its label, confidence and X Y Z position

scenes.caption: Review the scan. Export a file you own.
scenes.narration: Review everything the scan found, then export it as a file you own.
scenes._editNote:
Was two shots: `review-panel-empty` (the panel before any capture) then `review-export-panel` (the panel with objects in it). The empty one is gone, and the reason is what it did to the narration. The line is "Review everything the scan found" — and for the first half of the beat it played over a panel reading "No objects yet. Tap the capture button to scan.", with Export GLB greyed out. The film said one thing and showed its opposite.

Worse in sequence: the scene BEFORE this one (`objects-named`) already shows the detections panel full of named objects. Going full -> empty -> full in the middle of the story reads as the app losing the scan, not as a before-and-after. A before-and-after also has no work to do here; nobody watching needs to be told an empty app is empty.

The shot was a valid, honest capture and the plate is not the problem — it was pointed at the wrong moment. Its PNGs are deleted with it rather than left orphaned in assets/shots.

shots.alt: The same panel after a capture, with the object list filled in and GLB export, summary export and server-processing actions in the footer

scenes.caption: Every room, one world, your server.
scenes.narration: Every room you scan lands in one 3D world, stored on your own server.

shots.alt: The World Editor with three room scans listed in the sidebar, each one ready and optimized, and the camera framed on the selected room
The same world after picking the second room from the sidebar: the camera has flown to that scan and the Edit tab has opened on its name, confidence and tags

scenes.caption: Named objects, not an anonymous point cloud.
scenes.narration: The map is not just geometry. Every object keeps the label it was given.

shots.alt: Semantic view of the same world, colouring the scene by the label attached to each detected object

scenes.caption: Preview, Reconstructed, Photoreal — and what each tier needs.
scenes.narration: Three tiers of map quality, and the app names what the next one needs: keyframes, streamed while you scan.

shots.alt: The Layers tab showing the Map Quality stepper — Preview, Reconstructed, Photoreal — with the selected scan's current tier lit and the next step spelled out

scenes.caption: Local capture, self-hosted pipeline.
scenes.narration: It runs in the browser on your phone and sends scans to your own server.
Companion Scan, from Companion Intelligence. UnCloud your life.
